gaps.sentence: 'Are you coming to the party?' they asked me. They asked ___ coming to the party.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions become if/whether clauses; pronouns and tenses shift: if I was coming.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you finished the report?' the boss asked. The boss asked ___ finished the report.
gaps.hint: present perfect → past perfect in a yes/no question
gaps.explanation: Have you finished → whether/if I had finished; statement word order throughout.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't touch the wet paint,' the caretaker warned us. The caretaker warned us ___ the wet paint.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands become not to + infinitive after told/asked/warned.

gaps.sentence: 'What time does the bank open?' she asked. She asked what time the bank ___.
gaps.explanation: The question reverts to statement word order and the verb backshifts: opens → opened.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Where do you live?' he asked me. He asked me where I ___.
gaps.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order, and present simple backshifts: do you live → I lived.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget your tickets,' she said to us. She ___ us to take our tickets.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' maps onto remind + object + to-infinitive.
